title: Coefficient biduality at finite and integral stages
statement:
For the coefficient stages of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and
[def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the following distinctions hold.

1. If $\Lambda=A_{E,n},E$, or
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, then $\Lambda$ is self-injective and
quasi-Frobenius. Ordinary duality $\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(-,\Lambda)$
is exact, preserves finite modules, and for every finite
$\Lambda$-module $M$ the evaluation map
$$
M\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda\bigl(\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(M,\Lambda),\Lambda\bigr)
$$
is an isomorphism. Consequently derived coefficient duality is an
anti-equivalence on bounded complexes with finite cohomology.
1. The discrete valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ is not
quasi-Frobenius. Ordinary evaluation is an isomorphism for finite
projective $R$-modules, but not for all finite $R$-modules.
Every $K\in D^b(R)$ with finite cohomology is perfect, and the
*derived* evaluation
$$
K\longrightarrow
R\operatorname{Hom}_R\bigl(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,R),R\bigr)
$$
is an isomorphism.
1. More generally, derived evaluation into the coefficient double dual
is an isomorphism for every perfect complex over any ring. In particular,
the finite-Tor point case does not require self-injectivity of the
coefficient ring.

Conventions: rings and coefficient modules here are commutative-ring coefficients with ordinary algebraic module duals. A finite module means finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. A self-injective ring is injective as a module over itself (the extension condition in [lem-sf-baer-criterion]); a commutative quasi-Frobenius ring means an Artinian self-injective ring, where Artinian means that descending chains of ideals stabilize. Perfect has the meaning of [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and derived Hom is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. The coefficient rings are those constructed in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. The finite-Tor point assertion uses bounded finite-cohomology point complexes, with finite Tor amplitude as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

proof.text: Extract the DVR structure, nonzero maximal ideal and its chosen uniformizer generator from extension_integers_dvr. The generator is nonzero because its ideal is nonzero, hence irreducible because its principal ideal is maximal. Rewrite the coefficient ideal power as the ideal generated by the power. The finite coefficient quotient has a finite underlying set, and is therefore Artinian and Noetherian. Fields are Artinian and Noetherian.

proof.text: Use the already proved source-library theorem IsDiscreteValuationRing.injective_quotient_pow for self-injectivity of a uniformizer-power quotient. Its proof classifies quotient ideals and extends each linear map by multiplication (Baer criterion). For fields use Module.injective_of_isSemisimpleRing. Given a short exact sequence, the dual kernel equals the annihilator of the original image, and the dual image equals the annihilator of the original kernel. Injectivity extends each functional across the inclusion, proving surjectivity of restriction.

proof.text: A finite module over the finite coefficient ring has a finite underlying set. Its dual embeds into the finite set of functions to the ring, so is finite. Apply the already proved IsDiscreteValuationRing.isReflexive_quotient_pow, whose proof decomposes a finite torsion module over the DVR into cyclic summands, proves evaluation invertible on each cyclic quotient using the annihilator calculation, then transports finite-product reflexivity. For fields finite-dimensional vector-space duality gives finite duals and invertible canonical evaluation.

source.place: Tags 0AVF, 066Z, 066U, 07VI and 0A66; source-library and Mathlib proof route described explicitly.

proof.text: At a field, bounded finite cohomology is equivalent to perfectness by the already proved DerivedCategory.isPerfect_iff. The dual of a perfect object is perfect, hence again bounded with finite cohomology, and canonical evaluation is invertible by DerivedCategory.IsPerfect.isIso_toIhomIhomUnit. ObjectProperty.liftDualEquivalence restricts the internal-Hom functor and gives the required equivalence and identity comparison with its ambient functor.

source.place: Tags 0AVF, 066Z, 066U, 07VI and 0A66; source-library and Mathlib proof route described explicitly.

proof.text: At the finite coefficient ring A apply the separate bounded dualizing-complex theorem with Omega equal to the derived tensor unit. The injective model is A in degree zero, whose degree-zero term is injective by Step 2 and whose other terms are zero. It is bounded in [0,0]. This model is also perfect, so the unit has finite cohomology. The scalar-action map is the curry of its right unitor; unitors_equal and MonoidalClosed.unitNatIso identify it with the hom of an isomorphism. The theorem therefore supplies precisely the requested restricted internal-Hom anti-equivalence.

The integral DVR is not Artinian: in an Artinian domain every nonzero element is a unit, contradicting the irreducible uniformizer. Thus it is not Artinian and self-injective. Finite projectives have invertible ordinary evaluation by Mathlib finite-projective reflexivity. The finite module R/(pi) is not reflexive by the already proved IsDiscreteValuationRing.not_isReflexive_quotient: every map to the domain R vanishes, whereas the quotient is nonzero.

proof.text: For a finite module M over the integral PID, choose a surjection from a finite free module using Module.Finite.exists_fin'. Its kernel is finite by Noetherianity and free by Module.free_of_finite_type_torsion_free'. Map the resulting short exact sequence into degree-zero complexes. The mapping cone of the inclusion is perfect, since both its source and target have bounded finite-projective terms, and its comparison to M[0] is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus each cohomology object of a bounded finite-cohomology complex is perfect. Apply perfect-cohomology assembly to obtain perfectness of the complex.

proof.text: The definition of coefficientDerivedEvaluation is the canonical MonoidalClosed.toIhomIhomUnit for the named derived braiding. Rewrite by this definitional equality and apply the already proved DerivedCategory.IsPerfect.isIso_toIhomIhomUnit. This proves evaluation for every perfect complex over every commutative ring and, with Step 7, the integral derived assertion. The named braiding and local irreducibility attributes keep elaboration from unfolding the derived monoidal structures.

proof.text: At a finite coefficient stage use finiteness of the ring to install Noetherianity. Apply the already proved source-library theorem DerivedCategory.isPerfect_of_finiteTorAmplitude to boundedness, finite cohomology and finite Tor amplitude. Unpack its bounded finite-projective witness into IsPerfectRingComplex and apply Step 8. This avoids the separate finite-stage finite-free-model lemma; no self-injectivity is needed.
